prompt: The client claims their "Quality Processes" practice has reached the top maturity level (7) described in the context — the most advanced stage in this area. As their advisor, what would you check before accepting that claim, and how would you recommend they defend and extend this advantage over the next 12 months?
context:
Digital Processes — Quality Processes — excerpt from a client diagnostic interview:
"AI algorithms determine the scope of quality control in the production process for efficient and precise management of the quality control process. These algorithms use data analysis and product quality histories to automatically determine which production batches require detailed quality control."

The team says this reflects digital maturity level 7 of 7 ("AI Support").

binaryCriteria.description: Does not accept the client self-report at face value; explicitly asks for a concrete, checkable artifact before confirming the maturity level.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Satisfied if the answer requests something like: Evidence: an AI quality-prediction report with precision/recall for the last 90 days; a log of batches released without full inspection based on an AI recommendation (and their outcomes); a calculation of costs avoided …

binaryCriteria.description: Identifies a concrete, correct next step or defensive move consistent with the next maturity stage (or, for a top-level claim, a concrete way to defend/extend it) — not a generic "digitize more" platitude.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Must name a specific mechanism, system, or practice, not a vague call to "improve digitally".

binaryCriteria.description: The recommendation is grounded in the specifics of the client's described current practice, not a copy-paste generic maturity answer that ignores the actual tools/process mentioned in the context.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the answer could be pasted unchanged into any other maturity area without modification.

goldNotes:
Expert verification probes: Show us how an AI algorithm decides which production batches need a full quality inspection versus which can be released based on process data. | How does AI predict defects before they occur — with how much lead time, and with what accuracy over the last 90 days? | Describe a case where an AI quality prediction avoided a complaint or a costly rework — what was the savings metric?
What satisfies the evidence bar: Evidence: an AI quality-prediction report with precision/recall for the last 90 days; a log of batches released without full inspection based on an AI recommendation (and their outcomes); a calculation of costs avoided thanks to the prediction. Signal: AI-driven sampling has replaced calendar-based or 100% inspection on at least one line.
This is the highest defined level in this area — there is no "level 8"; the expected answer is about defending/deepening the advantage, not another checklist deployment.
Relevant technology categories: ML Models, QMS, MES, Machine Vision, IoT Data Feeds
